title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: Membership is the most important item we sell.
epigraph.author: Ron Vachris, President & CEO, Costco Wholesale (Q4 FY2026 Earnings Call)

web_blocks.html: Costco reports its business across three geographic operating segments: United States, Canada, and Other International [6, 13]. All three run the same membership-warehouse model [6, 13]. In FY2026 (52 weeks ended August 30, 2026), total revenue reached $303,154 million [7]. That total comprised $297,247 million in net sales and $5,907 million in membership fees [7]. The U.S. remains the anchor at 72.5% of total revenue ($219.8 billion) and 65.0% of operating income ($7.6 billion) [6, 14]. International operations, including Canada, punched well above their weight. They generated 27% of net sales and 35% of consolidated operating income [6, 14].

Concrete U.S. Segment Example: California alone accounts for roughly 26% of U.S. net sales [6, 15]. A suburban family in Issaquah, Washington or Orange County pays $130 per year for an Executive membership [6, 15]. On a Saturday morning, they fill a 20-gallon tank at the warehouse gas station for $0.25–$0.40 per gallon below local pumps. They pick up a 90-day prescription at Costco Pharmacy and load a flatbed cart with Kirkland Signature organic olive oil. They add a $4.99 rotisserie chicken and a 65-inch OLED television. At year-end, they earn a 2% annual reward (up to $1,250) on qualified purchases [6, 15].

Concrete Canada Segment Example: Across 115 Canadian warehouses (16.6 million sq ft), Costco commands high household penetration [6, 14]. Canada also delivers stronger operating margins at 5.17%, compared with 3.46% in the U.S. [6, 14]. A small restaurant operator in Toronto uses a Business Membership to buy case-pack beef, cheese, and paper disposables. By adding Kirkland Signature coffee beans to the cart, the owner bypasses traditional foodservice distributors.

Concrete Other International Segment Example: Costco operates 177 warehouses across 12 other countries [13]. The largest markets are Mexico (43), Japan (37), the U.K. (29), Korea (20), Australia (15), Taiwan (14), and China (7) [13]. Costco adapts local assortments while keeping its global playbook intact [13]. In Mexico or Japan, a member buys imported U.S. prime beef and Kirkland Signature nuts alongside fresh sushi platters or regional bakery items. Newer warehouses in Spain (5), France (3), Sweden (2), and China continue to draw strong initial sign-up surges [5, 13].

web_blocks.caption: Costco FY2026 Geographic Segment Breakdown (52 Weeks Ended August 30, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Canada and Other International together generate 27.5% of revenue but ~34.5% of segment operating income. Costco's unit economics clearly travel profitably across borders.

web_blocks.title: 2.2 Merchandise Categories, Ancillary Businesses & Membership Fees

web_blocks.html: Within its warehouses and e-commerce sites, Costco splits net sales into four merchandise and service verticals. A fifth standalone line captures membership fees [13, 14]:

1. Foods & Sundries ($116.8B, 39.3% of FY2026 net sales, +6.6% YoY): This category covers dry groceries, snacks, beverages, alcohol, cleaning supplies, and paper goods [14]. Concrete example: A regional beverage bottler ships full truckloads of sparkling water straight to Costco's cross-docking depots. Pallets move onto the warehouse floor in multi-pack cases with zero individual-unit shelf-stocking labor.

2. Non-Foods ($77.4B, 26.0% of net sales, +8.7% YoY): This vertical spans electronics, appliances, apparel, jewelry, patio furniture, and hardware [14]. It also houses Costco's signature 'treasure-hunt' rotating SKUs [14]. Concrete example: A member enters for paper towels and leaves with a seasonal Dyson vacuum or a limited-run designer jacket priced 30% below department stores.

3. Fresh Foods ($41.7B, 14.0% of net sales, +9.8% YoY): Fresh Foods includes meat, produce, deli, bakery, and prepared meals [14]. Concrete example: Costco's vertically integrated poultry complex in Fremont, Nebraska supplies millions of $4.99 rotisserie chickens. Management places this deliberate loss leader at the back of the warehouse so shoppers walk past higher-margin general merchandise.

4. Warehouse Ancillary & Other ($61.4B, 20.7% of net sales, +19.9% YoY): Gasoline (~11% of total net sales across 750+ stations) anchors this group [6, 13, 14]. It also includes Pharmacy, Optical, Hearing Aids, Food Court ($1.50 hot dog combo), Tire Centers, Business Centers, Costco Travel, and E-Commerce [6, 13, 14]. Concrete example: Digitally-enabled sales surpassed $33 billion in FY2026 (+20.9% YoY) [7, 16]. That volume spans Costco.com appliances, Costco Travel cruise packages, and sub-one-hour grocery delivery via Instacart, Uber Eats, and DoorDash [7, 16].

5. Membership Fees ($5,907M, 1.95% of total revenue, +11.0% YoY): Costco collects these fees upfront from 84.1 million paid households [6, 7]. That base includes 42.3 million Executive members, who drive 75.2% of net sales [6, 7]. Fees are recognized ratably over 12 months with virtually no cost of goods sold [6, 7]. As a result, $5,907 million of fee income equals 50.6% of Costco's $11,685 million consolidated operating income [6].

web_blocks.takeaway: Costco's merchandise categories generate massive scale at an 11.09% gross margin. Meanwhile, the 1.95% membership fee line provides half of consolidated operating profit.

web_blocks.html: Underlying every merchandise category is Kirkland Signature, which spans over 600 SKUs [4]. Items range from extra-virgin olive oil and golf balls to batteries and cashmere sweaters, generating roughly a third of company sales [4]. On the membership side, Costco offers two core tiers in the U.S. and Canada [6, 15]. Gold Star / Business costs $65/year and includes one free household card [6, 15]. Executive costs $130/year and earns a 2% annual reward up to $1,250 [6, 15]. Executive members represent 50.3% of paid members yet generate 75.2% of worldwide net sales. The 2% rebate incentivizes them to consolidate discretionary, travel, and grocery spend inside Costco [6].

web_blocks.title: 2.4 Kirkland Signature Co-Development & High-Frequency Ancillary Anchors

web_blocks.html: Kirkland Signature's ~$90 billion-plus scale is built on direct supplier co-development rather than generic white-labeling [4]. In Fresh Foods, Costco backed a dedicated poultry processing complex in Fremont, Nebraska [4, 14]. Controlling feed formulation, hatchery logistics, and plant throughput keeps its 3-pound rotisserie chicken at $4.99 [4, 14]. In packaged staples and hardlines, Costco pairs with leading producers to make Kirkland Signature AA/AAA batteries and single-origin Mediterranean olive oil. Buyers reverse-engineer specifications from the target member price backward. They strip out redundant distributor layers and bespoke retail cartons to lock in quality and cost.

Costco's ancillary businesses convert occasional bulk shoppers into habitual monthly visitors [6, 13]. Costco Pharmacy and Optical operate at razor-thin markups [16]. They dispense high-volume 90-day maintenance prescriptions and fabricate eyewear far below traditional optical-chain prices [16]. In FY2026, AI-driven pharmacy inventory optimization helped drive mid-teen script growth [16]. Meanwhile, Costco Travel operates as an asset-light digital brokerage for cruises, rental cars, and resort packages. It bundles Costco Shop Cards and room upgrades that accelerate a household's 2% Executive reward without tying up working capital [6, 15].

book_paragraphs: To see how Costco's machine actually works, you and I have to stop thinking of it as a single store and instead look at two distinct engines bolted onto the same chassis. The first engine is a $297.2 billion merchandising machine that deliberately earns almost nothing on the goods it sells—keeping an 11.09% gross margin and spending 9.15% on store and overhead expenses, leaving just 1.94% in pure retail operating profit. The second engine is a $5.91 billion annual subscription business that collects $65 or $130 upfront from 84.1 million households and drops almost every dollar straight to the operating line.

Let's walk through how the three geographic segments support that dual engine. In the United States, where 647 warehouses generated $219.8 billion in FY2026 revenue, California alone accounts for roughly a quarter of domestic net sales. Picture an Executive member in suburban Los Angeles: she pays $130 a year, fills up her SUV at the Costco gas pump for 30 cents a gallon below the corner station, picks up her family's prescriptions at the pharmacy, and wheels out a flatbed loaded with Kirkland Signature paper towels, fresh salmon, and a seasonal patio set. By the end of the year, her 2% Executive reward check alone covers the membership fee.

Now cross the border into Canada, where 115 warehouses generated $40.6 billion in revenue and $2.1 billion in operating income—a 5.17% operating margin that easily beats the U.S. average of 3.46%. In Canada, Costco is woven so deeply into household and small-business routines that an independent cafe owner in Montreal uses a Business Membership to source bulk dairy, coffee beans, and takeout containers every week. Meanwhile, across 177 Other International warehouses—from 43 locations in Mexico and 37 in Japan to 29 in the U.K. and 7 in China—Costco pairs imported American staples with local fresh foods, generating $42.8 billion in sales and $1.9 billion in operating profit.

book_subsections.title: Inside the Four Merchandise Verticals & Kirkland Signature
paragraphs: On the warehouse floor, those dollars split into four clear buckets. Foods and Sundries is the bedrock at $116.8 billion, or 39.3% of net sales, moving full pallets of dry groceries, beverages, and cleaning supplies straight from cross-docking trucks onto the concrete floor. Non-Foods contributes $77.4 billion (26.0%), powered by rotating 'treasure-hunt' pallets of electronics, apparel, and appliances that keep members scanning every aisle because an item spotted today might be gone next month.

Fresh Foods adds $41.7 billion (14.0%), anchored by vertically integrated operations like Costco's Fremont, Nebraska poultry complex that keeps the famous rotisserie chicken at $4.99—positioned at the very back of the building so you walk past higher-ticket items on your way to dinner. Finally, Warehouse Ancillary and Other is the fastest-growing bucket at $61.4 billion, up 19.9% in FY2026 to reach 20.7% of net sales. That line houses Costco's 750-plus gas stations (about 11% of total company net sales), pharmacies, optical and hearing-aid centers, tire shops, the $1.50 food court, Costco Travel, and an e-commerce business whose digitally-enabled sales crossed $33 billion in FY2026.

Tying all four verticals together is Kirkland Signature, Costco's ~$90 billion-plus private label. When you buy Kirkland Signature olive oil, AA batteries, or golf balls, you get quality benchmarked to the leading national brand at 20% to 40% less—while Costco earns up to 15% gross margin instead of 14%. Every ancillary service and every Kirkland Signature staple is engineered to give you one more reason to drive onto the lot, and once you are on the lot, the 92.3% North American renewal rate takes care of itself.

book_subsections.title: How Kirkland Signature Co-Develops Products From the Pallet Backward
paragraphs: When you hear 'private label,' you might picture a grocery chain slapping a generic sticker onto a second-tier manufacturer's leftover capacity. Kirkland Signature works the exact opposite way. Costco's buyers start with the best-selling national brand in a category, test it blind until they match or beat its quality, and then co-engineer the entire production run from the pallet backward. Take Kirkland Signature batteries or extra-virgin olive oil: Costco partners with top-tier producers, guarantees massive single-SKU volume, eliminates middleman brokers and flashy retail boxes, and passes the savings straight to you at 20% to 40% below the branded equivalent.

Nowhere is that commitment clearer than in Fremont, Nebraska. When rising poultry costs threatened the famous $4.99 rotisserie chicken, Costco didn't raise the price to $6.99 like a normal grocer. Instead, it invested in a vertically integrated poultry complex in Nebraska—overseeing everything from feed mills to processing lines—so it could lock in supply and cost for millions of chickens a year. Placing those steaming $4.99 chickens at the very back of every warehouse isn't an accident; it guarantees you walk past seasonal electronics, Kirkland Signature apparel, and fresh bakery displays on your way to dinner.

book_subsections.title: Why Pharmacy, Optical, and Costco Travel Lock In the Household
paragraphs: Look at how the ancillary businesses reinforce that habit. A traditional supermarket wants your weekly grocery basket, period. Costco wants your gasoline, your tires, your eyeglasses, your prescriptions, and your family vacation. When you pick up a 90-day prescription at Costco Pharmacy—where AI-assisted inventory tools helped drive mid-teen script growth in FY2026—or order progressive lenses at Costco Optical for a third of what a mall eyewear chain charges, you are already inside the building every few weeks.

Costco Travel takes that same trust online with virtually zero inventory risk. Because Costco is simply brokering cruises, rental cars, and resort packages on behalf of major travel suppliers, it doesn't own a single airplane or hotel room. Yet by negotiating exclusive member perks—like onboard credits or a Costco Shop Card mailed after your trip—Costco turns a $4,000 family vacation into an $80 Executive reward check, which pays back more than half of your $130 annual membership fee in one booking.

Think about what that dual-engine architecture means for you as an analyst trying to model the business. Most retailers have to choose between being a high-margin specialty store or a low-margin discounter. Costco's Kirkland Signature co-development and its pharmacy, optical, and travel anchors let it operate as an 11%-gross-margin discounter on the warehouse floor while capturing high-margin subscription loyalty at the membership desk.

book_callouts.title: The 50/50 Profit Split Myth vs. Reality
book_callouts.text: You will often hear investors say Costco makes 'all' its profit from membership fees. The FY2026 10-K shows a more nuanced truth: membership fees ($5,907 million) equal 50.6% of operating income ($11,685 million), down from 57.8% in FY2021. The merchandise side itself now earns $5,778 million in operating profit before fees—meaning both engines are compounding.

book_callouts.title: Ancillary Businesses Are Retention Engines, Not Side Hustles
book_callouts.text: Every ancillary service—gasoline, pharmacy, optical, hearing aids, tire centers, and Costco Travel—gives a member one more reason not to cancel. Once a household relies on Costco for fuel, prescriptions, and eyeglasses, switching to a rival club feels like uprooting three separate routines at once.
